extracted.intended_audience: public companies, investor relations professionals, securities counsel, and investors
extracted.subtask_description: Explains the purpose and basic compliance approach for Regulation FD (fair disclosure), including the use of Form 8-K Item 7.01 (or Item 8.01) to publicly disclose material non‑public information and example topics that have been filed under this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Regulation FD (fair disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of Regulation FD—for "fair disclosure"—is to prevent companies from selectively disclosing material, non-public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation FD is intended to level the playing field: companies generally must give material information to the public at the same time they provide it to others, such as securities market professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies generally must give material information to the public at the same time they provide it to others (e.g., securities market professionals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simultaneous/public-timing requirement is the core compliance obligation under Regulation FD to avoid selective disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of compliance: use of Form 8-K (Item 7.01 or Item 8.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies may submit an 8-K under this item or Item 8.01 as one method of complying with the public disclosure requirement of Regulation FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an 8-K under Item 7.01 (or Item 8.01) is a commonly used mechanism to publicly disclose material information in order to meet Regulation FD obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of disclosures commonly filed under Item 7.01
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual examples of 8-Ks filed under this item address a wide range of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include announcements of dividends, quarterly sales figures, or other business developments — i.e., material corporate information that, if selectively disclosed, would trigger Regulation FD concerns.
